# platform-orchestrator_plugin_enablement (Resource)

Enables a plugin installation for the provider's organization: the Plugin Manager decision a platform team manages declaratively.

Creating the resource enables the organization. Destroying it disables the organization, which keeps the plugin safety-only: cancel, rollback and reconciliation of plugin work in flight stay permitted, new work is refused. The enablement record with its timezone and approval policies stays; Terraform never removes it, because Core refuses even safety work of a plugin without one. An organization disabled outside Terraform is enabled again by the next apply.

Every change is a Plugin Manager command: the provider reads the installation, sends the Plugin Manager revision it read as `expected_revision` together with `reason`, and decides again on a fresh read when another change landed in between. A change whose target already holds writes nothing.

The installation must be active, or disabled installation-wide, before an organization can be enabled. An installation serves every organization it is enabled for, each with its own state, timezone and approval policies, and its identities belong to no organization, so any organization can be enabled. When the installation-wide licence grant limits the enabled organizations, enabling one beyond the limit is refused with `plugin_organization_limit`.

While the installation serves all organizations (`organization_mode` `all`, set by a platform operator with `octl plugin-manager organization-mode`), Core enables every organization itself, so the resource adopts the enablement Core created: creating it writes nothing when its settings already hold, and settings you configure replace the defaults. Destroying it disables the organization, which in that mode is the organization's opt-out: Core never enables it again, not when the mode is set again and not for a new organization. Removing the enablement is refused in that mode, which is why destroy disables. The mode itself is not managed by the provider.

The rest of the installation lifecycle (register the package, install, identities, activate, upgrade, disable, uninstall, reinstall, purge, organization mode) and licence imports stay Plugin Manager operator workflows in `v1alpha`, for example with `octl plugin-manager`. The provider's token needs the platform permissions `plugin_manager_read` and `plugin_manager_write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "platform-orchestrator_plugin_installation" "progressive_rollouts" {
  plugin_id = "dev.stellwerk.progressive-rollouts"
}

# The organization is the provider's org_id. In an installation that serves all organizations, Core created the enablement already; this resource adopts it.
resource "platform-orchestrator_plugin_enablement" "progressive_rollouts" {
  installation_id = data.platform-orchestrator_plugin_installation.progressive_rollouts.installation_id
  reason          = "Platform team adopts progressive rollouts for every application team"
  timezone        = "Europe/Berlin"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `installation_id` (String) The Core-assigned UUID of the plugin installation, for example from the `platform-orchestrator_plugin_installation` data source. Changing it disables the organization for the old installation and enables it for the new one.
- `reason` (String) Why the organization is enabled, at most 1000 characters. The Plugin Manager records it in the audit event of every change the resource makes, including the disable on destroy. Changing only the reason writes nothing; it is recorded with the next change. Import leaves it empty until the next apply.

### Optional

- `approval_policies` (Map of String) Deployment approval scope (`environment` or `project`) to the authorization policy of the plugin package that approves deployments in that scope. Unset keeps the current setting, none for a new enablement; `{}` removes all.
- `timezone` (String) The organization's IANA timezone for the plugin's calendar policies, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Unset keeps the current setting, `UTC` for a new enablement.

### Read-Only

- `plugin_id` (String) The plugin the installation belongs to.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the installation UUID; the organization is the provider's.
terraform import platform-orchestrator_plugin_enablement.progressive_rollouts "6f1c2a9e-8b3d-4c5e-9f7a-1b2c3d4e5f61"
```
